summary: Guidance: exclude internal monitoring probes from tenant burst budget without reducing burst capacity
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated 429 throttles during nightly orchestrator sweeps despite ample burst credits. Investigating whether internal monitoring/heartbeat probes are being counted against the tenant burst pool.

Impact:
- Production ingest jobs intermittently receive 429s during scheduled monitoring/telemetry sweeps.
- Latency-sensitive streaming clients experience short-lived degradation at sweep times.
- Customer is on a dedicated pool and expects monitoring probes not to affect burst allowance for production requests.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-novafleet-01 in prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- Redwood API via private VPC control plane
- Orchestrator and sidecars are in the customer VPC; healthchecks originate from an internal service mesh and a central monitoring cluster.

Observed behavior:
- Short windows (30–90s) of elevated 429s coincident with three scheduled telemetry sweep jobs (00:15, 02:15, 04:15 UTC).
- Console shows burst credits available but route-level token window drops to zero during sweeps.
- Logs sample attached below show many small concurrent probe requests (GET /v1/healthcheck) interleaved with long-poll streams.

Expected behavior:
- Healthcheck/monitoring probe requests should be accounted separately from production burst budget or routed to an exempted route/pool so they do not cause 429s for production traffic.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) On NovaFleet staging, schedule orchestrator sweep that hits 1000 endpoints over 60s.
2) Observe dedicated pool burst usage graph in Redwood Console.
3) Check /v1/responses for 429s for concurrent production streams.

Relevant logs (sanitized):
- 2026-03-10T00:15:03Z GET /v1/healthcheck 200 x-origin:mesh-prod x-probe-id:tm-001 12ms
- 2026-03-10T00:15:03Z POST /v1/generate 429 x-tenant:novafleet x-route:streams-lowlatency 4ms
- 2026-03-10T00:15:04Z GET /v1/healthcheck 200 x-origin:mesh-prod x-probe-id:tm-002 10ms
- 2026-03-10T00:15:05Z POST /v1/generate 429 x-tenant:novafleet x-route:streams-lowlatency 3ms

Additional notes:
- Customer has existing route separation for long-running streams and bulk uploads but healthchecks are sent to the default route.
- They use a service mesh sidecar that fans out probes to many internal IPs, causing a distributed microburst pattern.
- NovaFleet asks for prescriptive configuration and, if needed, a support-side change to exempt probes without losing overall burst protection on the tenant.
steps_to_reproduce: Schedule orchestrator sweep that hits ~1000 endpoints over ~60s
Observe dedicated pool burst usage in Redwood Console during sweep times
Monitor production client logs for transient 429s coincident with sweeps
suggested_workarounds: Create a dedicated route for healthchecks (e.g., /healthcheck) and assign to a low-priority, separate burst pool
Add a request header (X-Probe: yes) and set a route-level rule to map that header to an exempted or isolated quota in the ingress config
Throttle/fanout at the orchestrator level with jitter and worker-side backoff to smooth microbursts
Short-term: schedule sweeps in rolling windows (e.g., 10 batches) to avoid simultaneous fanout
support_investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 - Triage: Confirmed correlation between sweep windows and 429 spikes; console shows route-level token erosion even when tenant-level burst credit > 0
Reviewed ingress logs: probes are routed to default route and counted as production tokens
Checked dedicated-pool config: no existing route separation for mesh-originated probes
engineering_followup: Recommend small product change: allow 'probe' header to be mapped to a non-billable low-priority pool in the ingress rate-limiter rules (requires config release)
Raised INT-90821 to track internal schema addition for header-based probe-exempt routing
If customer prefers, we can support a tenant-scoped route that uses an isolated burst pool (requires support-assisted config change)
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah (Customer): We're seeing 429s at 00:15/02:15/04:15 UTC when our orchestrator runs sweeps. Console still shows burst credits; can you confirm probes are counted? Attached sanitized logs.

2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor (Support): Thanks Priya — triaging. We see correlated token erosion on the streams route during sweep windows. Two immediate options: isolate probes to a separate route/pool or add a header-based rule to classify probe traffic. We'll validate feasibility with Engineering.

2026-03-12 Taylor Nguyen (SRE): Confirmed probes hit default route. Short-term: recommend NovaFleet change orchestrator to add X-Probe: true header and fanout with jitter. Long-term: we can implement an ingress rule to map that header to an isolated burst pool; tracking in INT-90821.
2026-03-13 Priya Shah (Customer): Will try the header-based fanout change and stagger sweeps. Please keep INT-90821 open for a product-level exemption. ETA for customer verification: 2026-03-15.

2026-03-13 Liam O'Connor (Support): Noted — changing status to In Progress. Assigned Engineering follow-up and left recommended temporary mitigations. SLA note: follow-up with customer after they run staged sweep on 2026-03-15.
